comments.text: Every contribution to building a mosque, even a single stone given with sincere intention, is met with Allah's promise of a similar house in Paradise.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «أكثروا من ذكر هاذم اللذات» يعني: الموت
en.meaning: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Remember often the terminator of pleasures" - meaning death.

comments.text: At the peak of any worldly pleasure today, remember: there is a terminator of all pleasures that may arrive at any moment.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن تميم الداري رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «إن أول ما يُحاسب به العبد يوم القيامة من عمله صلاته، فإن صلحت فقد أفلح وأنجح، وإن فسدت فقد خاب وخسر»
en.meaning: Tamim al-Dari reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The first matter the servant will be called to account for on the Day of Resurrection is his prayer. If it was sound, he has succeeded and prospered; and if it was corrupt, he has failed and lost."

comments.text: The very first thing you will be asked about on the Day of Resurrection is your prayer - so put it right starting now.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «لا يشكر الله من لا يشكر الناس»
en.meaning: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "He who does not thank people does not thank Allah."
en.source: Sunan Abi Dawud / Jami' at-Tirmidhi Abu Dawud 4811, Tirmidhi 1954 — Sahih

comments.text: Before you claim gratitude to Allah, ask yourself: did you thank the last person who did you a kindness?

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن عبدالله بن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنهما أنه سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «من صلى عليّ صلاة، صلى الله عليه بها عشراً»
en.meaning: Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As reported that he heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say: "Whoever sends blessings upon me once, Allah will send blessings upon him tenfold."

comments.text: Every single blessing you send upon the Prophet right now, Allah returns to you tenfold.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن عدي بن حاتم رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «اتقوا النار ولو بشِقّ تمرة، فإن لم تجدوا فبكلمة طيبة»
en.meaning: Adi ibn Hatim reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Protect yourselves from the Fire, even with half a date; and if you cannot find that, then with a good word."
en.source: Sahih al-Bukhari / Sahih Muslim Bukhari 1417, Muslim 1016 — Sahih, agreed upon

comments.text: Do not belittle half a date given in charity - it may be your barrier against the Fire on the Day of Resurrection.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «من لم يدع قول الزور والعمل به، فليس لله حاجة في أن يدع طعامه وشرابه»
en.meaning: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever does not give up false speech and acting upon it, Allah has no need of him giving up his food and drink."

comments.text: Your hunger and thirst while fasting mean nothing to Allah if you do not also give up lying and false speech.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي أيوب الأنصاري رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «لا يحل لمسلم أن يهجر أخاه فوق ثلاث ليالٍ، يلتقيان فيُعرض هذا ويعرض هذا، وخيرهما الذي يبدأ بالسلام»
en.meaning: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari reported that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "It is not lawful for a Muslim to shun his brother for more than three nights, such that they meet and each turns away from the other; the better of the two is the one who initiates the greeting of peace."
en.source: Sahih al-Bukhari / Sahih Muslim Bukhari 6077, Muslim 2560 — Sahih, agreed upon

comments.text: If you have been avoiding someone for more than three days without valid religious reason, initiate peace today - the better of the two is whoever starts.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «من عال جاريتين حتى تبلغا، جاء يوم القيامة أنا وهو» وضمّ أصابعه
en.meaning: Anas ibn Malik reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever raises two girls until they reach maturity, he and I will come on the Day of Resurrection like this," and he joined his fingers together.

comments.text: Raising two orphaned girls until they reach maturity may place you right beside the Prophet himself on the Day of Resurrection.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «الجنة أقرب إلى أحدكم من شِراك نعله، والنار مثل ذلك»
en.meaning: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Paradise is closer to any of you than the strap of his sandal, and so is the Fire."

comments.text: The decision you make in this very moment may be as close as your sandal strap to either Paradise or the Fire.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن عبدالله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من قرأ حرفاً من كتاب الله فله به حسنة، والحسنة بعشر أمثالها، لا أقول {الم} حرف، ولكن ألف حرف، ولام حرف، وميم حرف»
en.meaning: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud reported that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever recites a letter from the Book of Allah receives a good deed for it, and a good deed is multiplied tenfold. I do not say that 'Alif-Lam-Mim' is one letter, but Alif is a letter, Lam is a letter, and Mim is a letter."

comments.text: Count the letters on the page you are reading right now - each single letter is worth ten complete good deeds.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «إن لله تسعة وتسعين اسماً، مائة إلا واحداً، من أحصاها دخل الجنة»
en.meaning: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred minus one; whoever encompasses them will enter Paradise."
en.source: Sahih al-Bukhari / Sahih Muslim Bukhari 2736, Muslim 2677 — Sahih, agreed upon

comments.text: Only ninety-nine names stand between you and the promise of Paradise - have you truly encompassed them with understanding and supplication, not just memorization?

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن ثوبان رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «استقيموا ولن تُحصوا، واعلموا أن خير أعمالكم الصلاة، ولن يحافظ على الوضوء إلا مؤمن»
en.meaning: Thawban reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Be upright, though you will never be able to fully account for it; and know that the best of your deeds is prayer, and none but a believer maintains ablution."

comments.text: Your diligence in maintaining ablution, even under difficult circumstances, is a hidden sign of the sincerity of your faith.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي زهير عمارة بن رويبة رضي الله عنه أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «لن يلج النار أحد صلى قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها» يعني الفجر والعصر
en.meaning: Umarah ibn Ruwaybah reported that he heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: "No one who prays before the sun rises and before it sets will enter the Fire" - meaning Fajr and Asr.

comments.text: These two prayers alone, Fajr and Asr, if you maintain them, the Prophet promised you will not enter the Fire.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن بريدة بن الحصيب رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «بشّر المشّائين في الظُّلَم إلى المساجد بالنور التام يوم القيامة»
en.meaning: Buraydah ibn al-Husayb reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Give glad tidings to those who walk to the mosques in darkness, of complete light on the Day of Resurrection."
en.source: Sunan Abi Dawud / Jami' at-Tirmidhi Abu Dawud 561, Tirmidhi 223 — Sahih

comments.text: Every step you take through the darkness toward the mosque today turns into complete light illuminating your way on the Day of Resurrection.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن البراء بن عازب رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «ما من مسلمين يلتقيان فيتصافحان، إلا غُفر لهما قبل أن يتفرّقا»
en.meaning: Al-Bara ibn Azib reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "No two Muslims meet and shake hands except that they are forgiven before they part."

comments.text: Your next handshake with a fellow Muslim may result in both of you being forgiven before you even part ways.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن معاذ بن جبل رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «من كان آخر كلامه لا إله إلا الله دخل الجنة»
en.meaning: Mu'adh ibn Jabal reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever's last words are 'There is no god but Allah' will enter Paradise."

comments.text: The last word you utter in this life could be the key to your Paradise - keep your tongue ready for it always.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن المقدام بن معدي كرب رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «ما أكل أحد طعاماً قط خيراً من أن يأكل من عمل يده، وإن نبي الله داود عليه السلام كان يأكل من عمل يده»
en.meaning: Al-Miqdam ibn Ma'dikarib reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "No one has ever eaten better food than that which he earns by the work of his own hands. Indeed, the Prophet of Allah, Dawud, peace be upon him, used to eat from the work of his own hands."

comments.text: If a prophet and king like David ate from the work of his own hands, no one has an excuse to feel shame in earning an honest living through their own effort.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن حكيم بن حزام رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «اليد العليا خير من اليد السفلى، وابدأ بمن تعول، وخير الصدقة عن ظهر غنى، ومن يستعفف يعفّه الله، ومن يستغنِ يُغنه الله»
en.meaning: Hakim ibn Hizam reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The upper hand is better than the lower hand. Begin with those you are responsible for. The best charity is that given out of surplus wealth. Whoever abstains from asking, Allah will keep him chaste; and whoever seeks self-sufficiency, Allah will make him self-sufficient."
en.source: Sahih al-Bukhari / Sahih Muslim Bukhari 1427, Muslim 1034 — Sahih, agreed upon

comments.text: Before giving charity to strangers, check: have you started with those under your care? This is what the Prophet taught us.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «تهادَوا تحابّوا»
en.meaning: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Exchange gifts, and you will love one another."

comments.text: Want to love someone more, or be loved more? Start with a simple gift - exchanging gifts is a direct cause of mutual love.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن معاذ بن جبل رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: قال الله عز وجل: «المتحابّون في جلالي لهم منابر من نور، يغبطهم النبيون والشهداء»
en.meaning: Mu'adh ibn Jabal reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said that Allah, Mighty and Sublime, said: "Those who love one another for My glory will have pulpits of light, and the prophets and martyrs will envy them."

comments.text: Loving your brother purely for Allah's sake may earn you a pulpit of light that even the prophets and martyrs will envy.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن معاذ بن أنس رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «من كظم غيظاً وهو قادر على أن يُنفذه، دعاه الله سبحانه وتعالى على رؤوس الخلائق يوم القيامة، حتى يُخيّره من الحور العين ما شاء»
en.meaning: Mu'adh ibn Anas reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever suppresses his anger while being able to act on it, Allah will call him before all of creation on the Day of Resurrection, until He lets him choose whichever of the maidens of Paradise he wishes."
en.source: Sunan Abi Dawud / Jami' at-Tirmidhi Abu Dawud 4777, Tirmidhi 2493 — Hasan

comments.text: Suppressing your anger right now, despite being able to retaliate, may cause Allah to call you before all of creation on the Day of Resurrection, letting you choose your reward.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن عبدالله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهما عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «الراحمون يرحمهم الرحمن، ارحموا من في الأرض يرحمكم من في السماء»
en.meaning: Abdullah ibn Amr reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Show mercy to those on earth, and He who is in heaven will show mercy to you."
en.source: Sunan Abi Dawud / Jami' at-Tirmidhi Abu Dawud 4941, Tirmidhi 1924 — Sahih

comments.text: Every act of mercy you extend to those on earth today returns to you from heaven in kind.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «من حسن إسلام المرء تركه ما لا يعنيه»
en.meaning: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Part of the excellence of a person's Islam is his leaving what does not concern him."

comments.text: Before you involve yourself in something that is none of your business today, remember: the excellence of your faith is measured by how well you leave it alone.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن تميم الداري رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «الدين النصيحة». قلنا: لمن؟ قال: «لله، ولكتابه، ولرسوله، ولأئمة المسلمين وعامتهم»
en.meaning: Tamim al-Dari reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Religion is sincere counsel." We said, "To whom?" He said, "To Allah, His Book, His Messenger, and to the leaders of the Muslims and their common folk."

comments.text: If you wanted to sum up your entire religion in one word, it would be: sincere counsel - are you giving it to Allah, His Book, His Messenger, and to fellow Muslims?

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «لا يؤمن أحدكم حتى أكون أحبّ إليه من والده وولده والناس أجمعين»
en.meaning: Anas ibn Malik reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "None of you truly believes until I am more beloved to him than his father, his child, and all people."
en.source: Sahih al-Bukhari / Sahih Muslim Bukhari 15, Muslim 44 — Sahih, agreed upon

comments.text: If you weighed your love for the Prophet against your love for those closest to you, which would truly come first in your heart?

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي قتادة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «من سرّه أن ينجيه الله من كرب يوم القيامة، فلينفّس عن معسر أو يضع عنه»
en.meaning: Abu Qatadah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever would like Allah to save him from the distress of the Day of Resurrection, let him grant respite to one in difficulty, or forgive him his debt."

comments.text: If someone owes you a debt and is in hardship, granting them respite or forgiving the debt may save you from the entire distress of the Day of Resurrection.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن عبدالله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «قد أفلح من أسلم، ورُزق كفافاً، وقنّعه الله بما آتاه»
en.meaning: Abdullah ibn Amr reported that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "He has succeeded who has submitted to Islam, been given sufficient provision, and been made content by Allah with what He has given him."

comments.text: If you are a Muslim, your provision is sufficient, and your heart is content with it, you are truly among the successful, however small your wealth may appear.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن عبدالله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «لا حسد إلا في اثنتين: رجل آتاه الله مالاً فسلّطه على هلكته في الحق، ورجل آتاه الله الحكمة فهو يقضي بها ويعلّمها»
en.meaning: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "There is no envy except in two cases: a man to whom Allah has given wealth and he spends it righteously, and a man to whom Allah has given wisdom, and he judges by it and teaches it."
en.source: Sahih al-Bukhari / Sahih Muslim Bukhari 73, Muslim 816 — Sahih, agreed upon

comments.text: If you are going to envy anyone, let it only be someone who spends wealth righteously, or spreads knowledge to others.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «لو يعلم المؤمن ما عند الله من العقوبة، ما طمع في جنته أحد، ولو يعلم الكافر ما عند الله من الرحمة، ما قنط من رحمته أحد»
en.meaning: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "If the believer knew the extent of Allah's punishment, no one would feel secure in hoping for His Paradise; and if the disbeliever knew the extent of Allah's mercy, no one would despair of His mercy."

comments.text: Do not be complacent about your good deeds and feel secure, nor despair of Allah's mercy however great your sins - both extremes are forbidden.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أحبّ الأعمال إلى الله أدومها وإن قلّ»، وقال: «كلّفوا من الأعمال ما تطيقون»
en.meaning: Aisha reported that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The most beloved of deeds to Allah are the most consistent, even if small," and he said, "Take on only as much as you can bear."
en.source: Sahih al-Bukhari / Sahih Muslim Bukhari 6465, Muslim 782 — Sahih, agreed upon

comments.text: A small good deed you sustain consistently is better with Allah than a large one you abandon quickly.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا عمل عملاً أثبته، وقال: «خذوا من الأعمال ما تطيقون، فإن الله لا يملّ حتى تملّوا»
en.meaning: Aisha reported that when the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, did a deed, he would maintain it consistently, and said: "Take on only as much of deeds as you can sustain, for Allah does not become weary until you become weary."
en.source: Sahih al-Bukhari / Sahih Muslim Bukhari 43, Muslim 782 — Sahih, agreed upon

comments.text: Your continuation in good deeds, even in small amounts, is what keeps the door open - do not be the one to close it first through your own fatigue.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي برزة الأسلمي رضي الله عنه قال: قلت: يا رسول الله، علّمني شيئاً أنتفع به. قال: «اعزل الأذى عن طريق المسلمين»
en.meaning: Abu Barzah al-Aslami reported: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, teach me something beneficial." He said, "Remove harmful things from the path of the Muslims."

comments.text: When the Companion asked for the most beneficial deed, the Prophet did not recommend a complex form of worship, but simply removing harm from the road.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن عثمان بن عفان رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «خيركم من تعلّم القرآن وعلّمه»
en.meaning: Uthman ibn Affan reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The best among you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it."

comments.text: The best of people is not the wealthiest or strongest, but the one who learns the Qur'an and then teaches it to others.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن عمران بن حصين رضي الله عنهما عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «الحياء لا يأتي إلا بخير»
en.meaning: Imran ibn Husayn reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Modesty brings nothing but good."
en.source: Sahih al-Bukhari / Sahih Muslim Bukhari 6117, Muslim 37 — Sahih, agreed upon

comments.text: If you ever think your modesty is holding you back from some benefit, remember: modesty brings nothing but good, however it may appear otherwise.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن سلمان الفارسي رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «لا يردّ القضاء إلا الدعاء، ولا يزيد في العمر إلا البرّ»
en.meaning: Salman al-Farisi reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Nothing repels the decree except supplication, and nothing increases lifespan except righteousness."

comments.text: Your supplication today may be the very cause Allah decreed to lift a hardship that was otherwise destined - so never abandon supplication.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «والذي نفسي بيده، لا تدخلون الجنة حتى تؤمنوا، ولا تؤمنوا حتى تحابّوا، أولا أدلّكم على شيء إذا فعلتموه تحاببتم؟ أفشوا السلام بينكم»
en.meaning: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I not guide you to something that, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread the greeting of peace among yourselves."

comments.text: Spreading the greeting of peace, to those you know and those you don't, is the practical key the Prophet pointed us toward for mutual love, then faith, then Paradise.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «حق المسلم على المسلم خمس: ردّ السلام، وعيادة المريض، واتباع الجنائز، وإجابة الدعوة، وتشميت العاطس»
en.meaning: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The right of a Muslim over a Muslim is five: returning the greeting, visiting the sick, following funeral processions, accepting invitations, and responding to one who sneezes."
en.source: Sahih al-Bukhari / Sahih Muslim Bukhari 1240, Muslim 2162 — Sahih, agreed upon

comments.text: Check today: have you fulfilled even one of these five rights owed to your fellow Muslims?

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «ادعوا الله وأنتم موقنون بالإجابة، واعلموا أن الله لا يستجيب دعاء من قلب غافل لاهٍ»
en.meaning: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Call upon Allah while being certain of a response, and know that Allah does not answer the supplication of a heedless, distracted heart."

comments.text: Your next supplication will not be answered if your heart is heedless and distracted - bring your heart to attention first, then call upon Him with certainty.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن عبدالله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن لله ملائكة سيّاحين في الأرض يبلّغوني من أمتي السلام»
en.meaning: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud reported that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Allah has traveling angels on earth, conveying to me the greetings of my nation."

comments.text: Your greeting of peace upon the Prophet right now, wherever you are, is carried by angels whose sole mission is exactly this.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «لا تسبّوا الأموات، فإنهم قد أفضوا إلى ما قدّموا»
en.meaning: Aisha reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Do not insult the dead, for they have already reached what they sent forth."

comments.text: Insulting someone who has died will not change their fate at all, but it will hurt the living who loved them - so leave it be.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «من رأى منكم منكراً فليغيّره بيده، فإن لم يستطع فبلسانه، فإن لم يستطع فبقلبه، وذلك أضعف الإيمان»
en.meaning: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri reported that he heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: "Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he cannot, then with his tongue; if he cannot, then with his heart, and that is the weakest degree of faith."

comments.text: If you cannot change a wrong with your hand or your tongue, at least reject it with your heart - that is the weakest degree of faith, not its absence.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «من يُرد الله به خيراً يُصب منه»
en.meaning: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whomever Allah wishes good for, He afflicts him with a trial."

comments.text: If misfortune befalls you, know that this very thing may be a sign that Allah has willed good for you.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن عبدالله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «الدنيا متاع، وخير متاع الدنيا المرأة الصالحة»
en.meaning: Abdullah ibn Amr reported that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "This world is provision, and the best provision of this world is a righteous woman."

comments.text: If you are searching for the best provision this world has to offer, the Prophet named it clearly: a righteous woman, not wealth or status.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «العمرة إلى العمرة كفّارة لما بينهما، والحج المبرور ليس له جزاء إلا الجنة»
en.meaning: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "An Umrah to the next Umrah is an expiation for what is between them, and the accepted Hajj has no reward except Paradise."
en.source: Sahih al-Bukhari / Sahih Muslim Bukhari 1773, Muslim 1349 — Sahih, agreed upon

comments.text: The accepted Hajj has a reward defined with precision: nothing less than Paradise itself.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «من حجّ لله فلم يرفث ولم يفسق، رجع كيوم ولدته أمه»
en.meaning: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever performs Hajj for Allah's sake and does not engage in obscenity or transgression will return as pure of sin as the day his mother bore him."
en.source: Sahih al-Bukhari / Sahih Muslim Bukhari 1521, Muslim 1350 — Sahih, agreed upon

comments.text: An accepted Hajj, free of obscenity and transgression, may return you as clean of sin as the day you were born.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «المستشار مؤتمن»
en.meaning: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The one asked for advice is entrusted."
en.source: Sunan Abi Dawud / Jami' at-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah Abu Dawud 5128 — Hasan

comments.text: If someone seeks your advice, you are entrusted with giving it honestly - do not flatter them at the expense of their true interest.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا ودّع رجلاً قال: «أستودع الله دينك، وأمانتك، وخواتيم عملك»
en.meaning: Abdullah ibn Umar reported that when the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, bid someone farewell, he would say: "I entrust to Allah your religion, your trustworthiness, and the conclusion of your deeds."

comments.text: Next time you say goodbye to someone traveling, try this prophetic supplication instead of the usual phrases: 'I entrust to Allah your religion, your trustworthiness, and the conclusion of your deeds.'

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «يسلّم الراكب على الماشي، والماشي على القاعد، والقليل على الكثير»
en.meaning: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The rider should greet the one walking, the one walking should greet the one sitting, and the smaller group should greet the larger group."
en.source: Sahih al-Bukhari / Sahih Muslim Bukhari 6231, Muslim 2160 — Sahih, agreed upon

comments.text: Next time you walk past someone who is sitting, remember: it is you who should greet them first.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن جابر بن عبدالله رضي الله عنهما عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «كل معروف صدقة، وإن من المعروف أن تلقى أخاك بوجه طلق، وأن تفرغ من دلوك في إناء أخيك»
en.meaning: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Every act of kindness is charity, and among acts of kindness is meeting your brother with a cheerful face, and pouring from your bucket into your brother's vessel."

comments.text: After all these hadiths, remember the unifying conclusion: every act of kindness - however small - is complete charity in Allah's sight.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن عبدالله بن عمر رضي الله عنهما عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «أعطوا الأجير أجره قبل أن يجفّ عرقه»
en.meaning: Abdullah ibn Umar reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Give the worker his wages before his sweat dries."

comments.text: If you employ a worker, hasten to pay their wages - the prophetic standard is precise: before their sweat even dries.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن معاوية بن حيدة القشيري رضي الله عنه قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «ويلٌ للذي يُحدّث بالحديث ليُضحك به القوم فيكذب، ويلٌ له، ويلٌ له»
en.meaning: Mu'awiyah ibn Haydah al-Qushayri reported that he heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: "Woe to the one who tells a story to make people laugh and lies in it; woe to him, woe to him."
en.source: Sunan Abi Dawud / Jami' at-Tirmidhi Abu Dawud 4990, Tirmidhi 2315 — Hasan

comments.text: If you lie in a story just to make people laugh, remember this warning repeated twice: woe to him, woe to him.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «كفى بالمرء كذباً أن يحدّث بكل ما سمع»
en.meaning: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "It is enough falsehood for a person to relate everything he hears."

comments.text: It is enough falsehood to relate everything you hear without verification - and this is exactly what this entire project has tried to avoid with every single hadith.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي الدرداء رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «من سلك طريقاً يلتمس فيه علماً، سهّل الله له به طريقاً إلى الجنة، وإن الملائكة لتضع أجنحتها لطالب العلم رضاً بما يصنع»
en.meaning: Abu al-Darda reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever takes a path seeking knowledge, Allah makes easy for him a path to Paradise; and the angels lower their wings for the seeker of knowledge, pleased with what he does."
en.source: Sunan Abi Dawud / Jami' at-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah Abu Dawud 3641, Tirmidhi 2682 — Hasan Sahih

comments.text: On every journey you take to seek sacred knowledge, imagine: angels lowering their wings beneath your feet, pleased with what you are doing.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن زيد بن ثابت رضي الله عنه قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «نضّر الله امرأً سمع مقالتي فوعاها، ثم أدّاها كما سمعها، فربّ مبلَّغ أوعى من سامع»
en.meaning: Zayd ibn Thabit reported that he heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: "May Allah brighten the face of a man who hears my words, retains them, and conveys them exactly as he heard them, for many a conveyer of knowledge conveys it to one more retentive than himself."
en.source: Jami' at-Tirmidhi / Sunan Abi Dawud and Ibn Majah Tirmidhi 2656 — Sahih

comments.text: The Prophet's prayer for radiance was for one who conveys his words with exact precision - and that is exactly what this entire project has tried to honor with every single hadith documented here.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «إذا مات الإنسان انقطع عمله إلا من ثلاث: صدقة جارية، أو علم يُنتفع به، أو ولد صالح يدعو له»
en.meaning: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "When a person dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, or a righteous child who prays for him."

comments.text: Invest in these three now: ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, or raising a righteous child - these alone continue after your death.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «الدنيا سجن المؤمن، وجنة الكافر»
en.meaning: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "This world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever."

comments.text: If this world feels confining to you, know that this very feeling is a sign of faith - it is the believer's prison on the way to a far greater Paradise.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «أحبّ البلاد إلى الله مساجدها، وأبغض البلاد إلى الله أسواقها»
en.meaning: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The most beloved places to Allah are the mosques, and the most disliked places to Allah are the marketplaces."

comments.text: In your city today, which place do you spend more time in: its mosques, beloved to Allah, or its marketplaces, disliked by Him?

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «الإيمان بضع وسبعون -أو بضع وستون- شعبة، فأفضلها قول لا إله إلا الله، وأدناها إماطة الأذى عن الطريق، والحياء شعبة من الإيمان»
en.meaning: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Faith has over seventy, or over sixty, branches. The most excellent of them is saying 'There is no god but Allah,' and the least of them is removing a harmful object from the road, and modesty is a branch of faith."
en.source: Sahih al-Bukhari / Sahih Muslim Bukhari 9, Muslim 35 — Sahih, agreed upon

comments.text: Every hadith you have encountered in this project was, in truth, a branch of this one comprehensive faith - from the declaration of monotheism to removing harm from a road.

en.title: Hadith
en.text: عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه في حديث جبريل الطويل، قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «الإحسان أن تعبد الله كأنك تراه، فإن لم تكن تراه فإنه يراك»
en.meaning: Umar ibn al-Khattab reported, in the long hadith of Gabriel, that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Excellence (ihsan) is to worship Allah as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then indeed He sees you."
en.source: Sahih al-Bukhari / Sahih Muslim Bukhari 50, Muslim 8 — Sahih, agreed upon

comments.text: After these two hundred hadiths, remember the unifying essence of them all: act in every moment as though you see Allah, and if you cannot achieve that, remember that He truly sees you.

en.title: Virtue of dhikr
en.text: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ
en.meaning: Glory be to Allah.
en.detail: Whoever says it one hundred times, one thousand good deeds will be recorded for him, or one thousand sins will be blotted out.

en.title: Virtue of dhikr
en.text: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ
en.meaning: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah.
en.detail: They fill what is between the heavens and the earth.

en.title: Virtue of dhikr
en.text: سُبْحَانَ اللهِ العَظِيمِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ
en.meaning: Glory be to Allah, the Magnificent, and praise be to Him.
en.detail: A date-palm tree is planted for him in Paradise.

en.title: Virtue of dhikr
en.text: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ، سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ
en.meaning: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him; glory be to Allah, the Magnificent.
en.detail: Two phrases that are light on the tongue, heavy in the scale, and beloved to the Most Merciful.

en.title: Virtue of dhikr
en.text: لا حَوْلَ وَلا قُوَّةَ إِلا بِاللَّهِ
en.meaning: There is no might or power except through Allah.
en.source: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim; Riyad as-Salihin 1443
en.detail: It is a treasure from the treasures of Paradise.

en.title: Virtue of dhikr
en.text: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ
en.meaning: Praise be to Allah.

en.title: Virtue of dhikr
en.text: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ
en.meaning: Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no deity except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest.
en.detail: This remembrance is among the speech most beloved to Allah, and it does not matter which of them one begins with.

en.title: Virtue of dhikr
en.text: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ
en.meaning: There is no deity except Allah.
en.detail: The best remembrance is: There is no deity except Allah.
